gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a Thunderbolt 4 certification or a 40Gbps rating does not guarantee 240W: Apple's own Thunderbolt 4 Pro Cable runs 40Gbps (Thunderbolt 4, Thunderbolt 3 and USB4) but delivers at most 100W, and Plugable says some Thunderbolt 4 cables stop at 100W. Thunderbolt 5 cables from Apple and Belkin, by contrast, carry 240W and work in Thunderbolt 4, Thunderbolt 3 and USB4 ports.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited Plugable product pages (usb4-240w-1m, tbt4-240w-1m) and ChatGPT's answer text. I couldn't open the two Plugable pages (plugable.com returned HTTP 429 every time), so I can't rule out that they mention it. ChatGPT's answer only says to look for 'Thunderbolt 4 with explicit 240W support' and that 'not every 40Gbps cable supports 240W'. It names no cable that fails, and it never says Thunderbolt 5 (80Gbps) cables also meet both requirements and work in older ports. The other results are listings of one product each (StarTech, ACT, Epico, Tripp Lite, Club 3D, resellers), and none of them is a cross-brand page about exclusions.
decides: It confirms the pick rule: a cable must state 240W itself, and the Thunderbolt 4 logo or a 40Gbps rating is not proof. It rules out the familiar Apple Thunderbolt 4 Pro Cable (100W max). It also adds Thunderbolt 5 cables to the shortlist, for example Belkin INZ005 at $53.99 on belkin.com: 240W, and Belkin lists Thunderbolt 4, Thunderbolt 3 and USB4 ports as compatible. ChatGPT did not show them.

findings.label: Max power (exclusion for 240W)
findings.value: 100 W maximum to any connected device, while running Thunderbolt 4, Thunderbolt 3 and USB4 at up to 40Gbps
findings.source_title: About the Apple Thunderbolt Pro Cables
findings.note: Apple quote: 'delivers a maximum of 100W power to any connected device'. So this is a 40Gbps Thunderbolt-logo cable that cannot do 240W.

findings.label: Power and backward compatibility
findings.value: 240 W maximum; Thunderbolt 5 up to 120Gbps; works in Thunderbolt 5, 4 and 3, USB4 and USB 3.2 Gen 2 (10Gbps) ports
findings.source_title: About the Apple Thunderbolt Pro Cables
findings.note: Apple quote: 'delivers a maximum of 240W power to any connected device'. Apple says charging works with Thunderbolt 5, 4 and 3 and USB-C devices. The page does not say whether the cable is passive or active.

findings.label: Thunderbolt 4 logo does not guarantee 240W
findings.value: Some Thunderbolt 4 cables stop at 100 W; others support up to 240 W
findings.source_title: Do Thunderbolt 4 Cables Support USB-C Power Delivery for Host Charging? (Plugable Knowledge Base)
findings.note: Plugable quote: 'some cables may not offer the full 240W capability and instead offer a maximum of 100W of Power Delivery'. The article was last updated 2023-03-13.

findings.label: Compatibility, power, price
findings.value: Works in Thunderbolt 5, 4 and 3, USB4 and earlier USB-C ports; up to 240 W; 80Gbps both ways (120Gbps one way with Bandwidth Boost); 1 m; $53.99; 2-year warranty
findings.note: SKU INZ005fq1MBK. Belkin calls it 'Thunderbolt 5 and Intel certified'. Price is on belkin.com as of 2026-11-17, and the page marks it not eligible for return. The page does not say what charger or device 240W requires.

findings.label: Active cable, 240 W, Thunderbolt 3 support
findings.value: Active, Intel-certified Thunderbolt 4 cable, 2 m (6.6 ft), 40Gbps, up to 240 W (PD 3.1); works with Thunderbolt 3 devices; USB4 speed 'depending on USB4 device and host compatibility'
findings.source_title: Cable Matters Active Thunderbolt 4 Cable with 240W Power Delivery Support, 6.6ft (Thunderbolt Technology product listing)
findings.note: This is a listing on the Thunderbolt technology site, not Cable Matters' own store page. ChatGPT's Cable Matters card ('40Gbps USB 4 Cable - 6.6ft') may be a different USB4 model, so match part numbers before linking. The image filename suggests part 107025-BLK, which I did not confirm.

unsourced: Compatibility statements and exclusions for Plugable USB4-240W-1M and TBT4-240W-1M (supported Thunderbolt 3 hosts, passive or active, what 240W EPR needs from the charger): plugable.com and plugable.com/en-ca returned HTTP 429 on every try, the Shopify storecheck also got 429, and device.report returned 403.

StarTech 1M-40G-USB4-CABLE datasheet: the PDF downloaded, but its text is compressed and the extractor could not read it; running pdftotext needed approval I didn't have. startech.com/en-us/cables/50c-40g-usb4-cable shows only a headline.

Club 3D CAC-1578 spec sheet: redirected to a login wall. ACT AC7451 page: returned no content. Epico UltraLink manual: 404. Tripp Lite U521 datasheet on Mouser: timed out.

Apple 240W USB-C Charge Cable data rate (to name a 240W cable that is USB 2 only): the Apple Store product page did not render. Apple's support page 118204 gives 480Mbps (USB 2.0) for its 'USB-C Charge Cable' without naming the 240W model, so I left it out.
Whether a passive 40Gbps cable longer than 1 m can be certified: I found no maker or USB-IF document stating the length limit.
